name: load_npc_schedules
purpose: Loads the settlement's NPC data. g_location is decremented in place; group = loc/8 picks towne.npc (DGROUP 0x6d46), dwelling.npc (0x6d50), castle.npc (0x6d5e) or keep.npc (0x6d6a); the 0x240-byte block (loc mod 8) is read in three parts: 0x200 bytes of schedules to 0x5d5e, 0x20 NPC types to 0x659e (offset +0x200) and 0x20 dialogue indices (offset +0x220) into a local buffer, each copied as a 16-bit value into NPC state +0xa (0x5f68 + 16*npc). g_location is incremented back at the end.

name: find_nearest_ladder
proto: int find_nearest_ladder(int npc, int want_up, int y, int x)
purpose: Wrapper around find_path_bfs with a negative mode: want_up != 0 -> mode -1 (goal = every ladder-up tile 0xc8), 0 -> mode -2 (ladder-down 0xc9); the search starts at (y, x) and returns 1 with g_dx/g_dy = the nearest ladder, 0 if none reachable. Ghidra param_1..4 = npc, want_up, y, x; a444 is the split-off else arm.

name: build_path_grid
proto: void build_path_grid(int npc, int mode, int gy, int gx, int sy, int sx)
purpose: Prepares the 32x32 pathing grid at *g_ool_buffer_ptr for NPC npc (schedule entry = schedule_index_for_hour(g_hour)). Each cell = 0 if npc_tile_passable(entry, npc, g_party_z, y, x) != 0 else 0x90; with mode -1/-2 every map tile 0xc8/0xc9 becomes a goal (5). Objects in monster slots 31..1 with tile >= 0x40 and the party (slot 0) within Manhattan distance < 4 of the NPC block their cell (0x90). mode >= 0: goal (gy, gx) = 5. Start (sy, sx) = 0x46 (visited + start marker 6; high nibble 4 = first expansion direction).

name: find_path_bfs
proto: int find_path_bfs(int npc, int mode, int gy, int gx, int sy, int sx)
purpose: Breadth-first search over the grid built by build_path_grid. Circular queue of 32 (x, y) entries; a dequeued cell is expanded in the four BFS directions starting with the direction in its own high nibble (1 x-1, 2 y+1, 3 x+1, 4 y-1) then rotating ((d&3)+1). A target cell with value < 0x10 gets dir<<4 and is enqueued (unless head == tail); if its low nibble was 5 the goal is found: g_dx/g_dy = cell, return 1. Queue empty -> 0. Quirks: bounds tests accept x == 0x20 / y == 0x20 (reads the next row / beyond the grid); queue indices wrap at 32.

0xb11c.name: g_ool_buffer_ptr
0xb11c.meaning: near pointer to the 1 KB scratch used as the 32x32 pathing grid

name: build_move_list
proto: int build_move_list(int y, int x, int mode, int npc)
purpose: Traces the BFS back from the goal (y, x): the cell's high nibble is the direction that reached it, so the trace steps the opposite way (1 -> x+1, 2 -> y-1, 3 -> x-1, 4 -> y+1), accumulating runs of equal direction as {count, dir} pairs in the NPC's move list (0x615e + 32*npc) until the start marker (low nibble 6) or 16 pairs. The list is reversed in place and directions converted to walking codes ((d+1)&3)+1 = 1 E, 2 N, 3 W, 4 S. Sets the read offset (0x655e + 2*npc) to 0 and returns the byte length. mode is unused.

name: npc_move_relative_party
purpose: Chase/flee step for AI types 3..7. Distance to the party's object slot (0x5c5c/0x5c5d) == 1 and AI > 3 -> contact: AI 4/5 with a non-zero dialogue index set g_npc_contact_kind = 't' (AI 4/5 with dialogue 0 move instead), AI 6/7 set 'a'; g_npc_contact_idx = npc. Otherwise the four walking directions are scored (99 = npc_can_move_to(-1, npc, ...) refused, else distance to the party after the step). AI 3: choose a direction with a larger distance (first one, later ones with 50%), stop at direction 4. Others: first direction with a smaller distance. The scan runs to 'direction' 7, reading past the 4-entry array (state pointer, current distance, AI type - never 99) and choosing direction 5..7 when candidate 1..3 equals the current distance; step_dxdy ignores 5..7 so the NPC stays. AI 5/7: 25% chance to switch to another enterable direction (each with 25% after the first). The step updates state x/y, the monster slot and g_view_dirty |= 2.

name: move_npcs
purpose: NPC movement turn (vector 1778:0339). Clears g_npc_contact_kind/idx. For NPCs 1..31 with a type: sched = schedule_index_for_hour. State <= 1 and check_schedule_change == 0: run_npc_ai when on the party's floor. Else state <= 3: follow the move list (one step; blocked -> stuck++, wander, drop the list after 4 blocks; step taken -> update position, count--, advance pairs, list ends -> 0xffff; npc_can_move_to == 2 (arrived) -> state 1, entry stored); no list: state 3 -> state 6/7 by target floor and RETURN from the whole function; if a BFS already ran this turn -> run_npc_ai(stored entry) when on floor; state 1 -> nothing; stuck < 200 and (stuck == 0 or 1/3 chance): BFS to the target (success: build list, stuck 0; failure: stuck = 200) then/else wander; stuck >= 200 counts up to 0xcd then 0. State 4/5 (once per turn): ladder nearest the target (0xc8/0xc9), BFS from the ladder to the target, build list, place_npc on the ladder if the map tile is that ladder or a stair 0xc4..0xc7, state 2. State 6/7 not on the right ladder (once per turn): BFS from the NPC to the nearest ladder (0xc8 for 6, 0xc9 for 7), list, state 3; on the ladder, or state 8: place_npc at the schedule target, entry stored, list 0xffff, state 1.
